set.descent_text: The second pitch finishes on top of the buttress. From there, walk off to the west.

review.notes: Route page states the walk-off west; area page gives the buttress context. Single source for the descent.

set.descent_text: The second pitch, up cracks on the steeper west-facing wall, reaches the top of the buttress. From there, walk off around to the west.

review.notes: Route page gives pitch 2 to the top and the walk-off west.

set.descent_text: The route ends on a large ledge near the top of the shield. Either rappel west from just below the ledge, using the tat and rap ring there, or keep scrambling up the broken ground above the ledge and walk down Big Blue.

review.notes: Route page lists both descents; keeps every fact of the stored text. Single source, no counts.

set.descent_text: The fourth pitch is low fifth-class ground to the ridge crest below the summit. To get off, walk to climber's right along obvious grassy ledges, with perhaps a fourth-class move or two.

review.notes: Route page for the walk-off and pitch 4 top-out; area page for the tundra caution (no maintained path).

set.approach: Park at the Glacier Gorge Junction trailhead, or ride the shuttle to it, and follow the Glacier Gorge trail past Mills Lake to Black Lake. Above the lake, head east on a faint path to treeline, then cut back south across slabs and meadows to the foot of the Spearhead's main southeast face. The route is the leftmost line on that face, with Border Patrol starting around the corner to its left.

review.notes: Spearhead area page for the approach beyond Black Lake; route page for position on the face; Arrowhead area page agrees on the Glacier Gorge-Mills-Black Lake trail. No descent set: the route page does not say where it tops out.

set.descent_text: Pitch 5 ends at chains on top of The Citadel. From those chains, one rappel down the north face reaches the ground, or the route itself can be rappelled. Another option is to walk a short way west and drop down the brushy gully to the base.

review.notes: Route page: top-out chains, rappel the route or one rappel down north face. Area page: single rappel from chains into the slot, or walk west and descend the gully.

set.descent_text: The fifth pitch ends on top of The Citadel, as Tempest does. From the chains up there, make one rappel down the north face into the slot, or rappel the line of the route. A walk-off also exists: go a short way west and descend the brushy gully to the base.

review.notes: Own page says to descend as for Tempest and tops out at the top of The Citadel, the same point where Tempest ends; Tempest page and area page give the descent.

set.descent_text: From the top, traverse east to the north-facing chute just east of the climb and descend it into the valley below.
set.approach: This is a remote north-facing buttress in a valley just south of Walk of Life Spire. From the pond and meadow below the scree field under that spire, follow the side valley that splits off to the south all the way back to the foot of The Stargate. The line follows the weakness just left of the centre of the buttress.

review.notes: Area and route pages agree on the descent chute east of the climb. Trailhead leg is not on the pages, so the approach starts at the meadow below Walk of Life Spire. No counts.

set.descent_text: Rappelling is the preferred way down, rather than hiking the Dinosaur Couloir, because it does less damage to the ground and the wildlife. The rappel anchors are behind the top-out. Tie knots in the rope ends, since the line may be longer than one rope reaches, then scramble down the gully to the base of the wall.

review.notes: Route page for the rappel descent; area page agrees you can rappel from the ridge or hike the gullies. No rope or rappel counts stated.

set.descent_text: Bring a 70 m rope. Rappel by way of the Road Warrior bolts down to the Master Blaster anchor, and from that anchor to the ground. Stay on those bolts all the way, because leaving that line puts the rappel over an overhang. From the second-pitch anchor, either belay up and scramble a short stretch of easy fifth class to the Road Warrior anchor, or clip that anchor and move up and right to it.
set.approach: The buttress stands on the west side of the road, directly across from the Stairway to Heaven parking lot, and the foot of it is a short hike straight up the scree. Bartertown starts a short way left of the buttress's bolted nose. It begins up a low-angle slab to reach the steep, overhanging walls above.

review.notes: Route page for the rappel line and the warning; Thunderdome area page agrees on 70 m rope and rappel descent, and gives the approach. No rappel count.
